The hook that never ran

PR playground for #4024: every feature push has been ungated, and it looked exactly like a passing hook.

Before and after, same branch, same command

before
Running pre-push validations for branch: fix/4024-prepush-runs-tests
  Skipping version check for fix/4024-prepush-runs-tests
                                          (push proceeds. nothing ran.)

after
  Running TypeScript type check... OK      Running security tests... OK
  Verifying build... OK                    Running mdx-compile guard... OK
  Verifying imports... OK                  Validating agent frontmatter... OK
  Running unit tests... OK (62 tests)      Validating skill structure... OK
                                           Checking manifests... OK
                                           Checking token overhead... OK
Pre-push validation passed

One statement, the wrong scope

if [[ "$BRANCH" =~ $VERSION_SKIP_PATTERN ]]; then
  echo "  Skipping version check for $BRANCH"
  exit 0          <- leaves the entire hook, not the version gate
fi

The message says version check. The statement leaves the script. And VERSION_SKIP_PATTERN matches every conventional-commit prefix CONTRIBUTING tells contributors to use, so the skip was not an exception. It was the default path, and a bare-named hotfix branch was the only shape still being tested.

What was hiding in the dead code

The runner discovers test-*.sh and test-*.mjs, then ran every one of them under bash:

bash tests/unit/test-import-symbols.mjs  -> rc=2  syntax error
node tests/unit/test-import-symbols.mjs  -> rc=0

Both .mjs unit tests were guaranteed failures the moment the runner executed. It never did, so nobody saw it. A dead code path is where bugs go to wait, and un-skipping the hook is what would have surfaced this as a mystery red on somebody else's push.

I predicted eleven blockers. There were two.

predictedmeasured
failing tests in the pre-push set112

The prediction extrapolated from a full npm test across 25 categories. Pre-push runs a much narrower set: integration, e2e, worktree and plugins are not in it, and they held most of those failures. The security suite passes now too, because the #4023 timeout fix landed. So the coupling to #4026 was real but one test wide, not nine.

Two self-corrections, both caught by checking

  • Typecheck first read FAIL. Stale local node_modules (vitest 4.1.11 installed, main pins ^5.0.0). After npm ci it passes. Main was never broken.
  • My measurement loop ran bash on .mjs, inflating 2 failures into 4. Caught only by checking exit codes individually. That mistake is what found the real dispatch bug above, so it is in the record rather than tidied away.

Proof the gate was not simply disabled

fix/4024-prepush-runs-tests  version gate skipped, suite runs   rc=0
hotfix-vgate-probe2          version gate RUNS, blocks       rc=1
  "Checking version bump... FAILED  Version not bumped!"

A bare-named branch still gets the version check, which is the behaviour #1457 put there. Only its scope changed.

Run it

bash tests/unit/test-prepush-interpreter-dispatch.sh
echo "refs/heads/$(git branch --show-current) $(git rev-parse HEAD) x $(git rev-parse origin/main)" \
  | bash bin/git-hooks/pre-push origin url
The flaky latency assert was fixed, not quarantined: it now measures a trivial prompt through the same hook in the same run and bounds the oversized one against it, so node startup and machine load cancel. #3522 class.
